notes: Behaviour patterns, not word lists. No slurs, no explicit material.
Phrase syntax: words separated by spaces. a|b = either word. * = up to three other words.
Text is lower-cased, apostrophes dropped, common leetspeak and chat shorthand (u, ur, r, pls) expanded before matching.
phrases score the category weight. weak phrases score 1.
A block is one read of a chat window. Combos add a bonus when two categories show up in the same block.
Tests must stay synthetic. Never add real chat logs here.
sources: NCMEC NetSmartz: online enticement and grooming warning signs
CEOP / Thinkuknow (UK): grooming stages, secrecy and platform moves
Discord Family Center and Safety Center guidance for parents
Roblox Safety and Parental Controls guidance (Robux lures, off-platform moves)

categories.label: personal information
categories.talkItOver: Ask who they were chatting with and whether they know that person in real life. A simple family rule helps: school, address, phone number, and last name stay private online.

categories.label: moving the chat to another app
categories.talkItOver: Ask if someone wanted to move the chat to a different app. People who push to switch apps are often trying to get away from the game's safety tools. It is always okay to say no.

categories.label: keeping secrets from parents
categories.talkItOver: Let them know that no one online should ask them to keep secrets from you, and that they will not be in trouble for telling you about it.
phrases: do your parents check your phone|messages|chats

categories.label: someone building trust too fast
categories.talkItOver: Free gifts, lots of flattery, or "no one gets you like I do" can be a way to build trust fast. Ask calmly how they know this person and what the person has offered them.
phrases: when do your parents get home|back

categories.label: meeting in person
categories.talkItOver: Ask about the plan without anger. A clear family rule works well: never meet someone from online without a parent there.
phrases: what time * get out of school

categories.label: requests for photos or private contact
categories.talkItOver: Stay calm and thank them if they tell you. They are not in trouble. If an adult asked a child for pictures, you can report it to the NCMEC CyberTipline at report.cybertip.org or to local police.
